commits.headline: feat(multiplayer): bolts are the host's, once in the world
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
Only the host's game drops bolts: its enemies' and its crates', a crate a member broke too (its
copy breaks for the member's BROKE and now drops). A member's game in the host's level drops none
of its own: Moby_RecordDeath records the death (its killed bits) with the drop left out. The host's
dropped bolts reach every member as before (SPAWN), posed from WORLD while they fly; once one has
landed in the host's game (bolt state 3: WORLD's new loose flag) the member's copy is no longer
driven and…

commits.headline: feat(multiplayer): the party shares items, gold bolts and planets
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
What one player gets, every player has: the items owned (weapons, gadgets, the packs; found,
given or bought), the gold bolts collected (and so their count) and the planets unlocked. Each game
reads them a few times a second (item_available, gold_bolts_collected, level_available on either
disc). A member tells the host what it has (PROGRESS, 23); the host gives its own game what a
member has that it lacks and tells everyone what the party has, at each change, at each member
that comes and every…

commits.headline: docs(multiplayer): the open decisions and the ones made
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body: Saving each player's progress, the game's own saves on members' cards, gameplay mods that differ from the host's, the randomizer seed, what progress is shared, the host leaving, mixed regions and the release steps, each with today's behaviour, the choices and a recommendation; and a table of what is already decided.

commits.author: Veradictus

commits.headline: fix(multiplayer): a bolt flies to the player nearest it
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
In the host's game a bolt could only fly to the host's Ratchet: the gate gave no stand-in to the
pickup classes, bolts among them, and a crate's drop starts flying to the hero at once. Nearly
every bolt, those of a member's crate too, was the host's. A bolt's update now has the nearest
player stand in for the hero, as an enemy's does: it flies to that member's figure, and collected
there it is that member's (BOLTS), with nothing added to the host's count and nobody's later
claim taking it…

commits.headline: feat(multiplayer): connect to game.openrac.dev by default
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body: The public OpenRAC server is the default; localhost:7770 is still a setting away for a server of one's own.

commits.headline: build: build against the mod SDK 1.10.0
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body: Interface 1.10 has the play, world and pause-menu calls multiplayer needs, so CI builds it again.

commits.headline: fix(multiplayer): a member's Ready stands against an older STATE from the host
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body: The host's STATE replaced the member's whole ready list, its own entry included. A STATE sent before the member's last toggle could arrive after it and put the old answer back, so the next toggle flipped the wrong way: Ready pressed twice quickly sent Not ready twice and the host never saw everyone ready. That was the multiplayer test failing on macOS CI. The host only changes a member's entry on that member's own READY, so the member keeps its own word.

commits.headline: chore(multiplayer): version 0.7.1
commits.author: Veradictus

commits.headline: fix(multiplayer): remote figures and the host's mobys move smoothly over a slow link
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The buffer played poses a fixed 2.5 send intervals behind their stamps, leaving out the time
they spend in transit. Through game.openrac.dev a WORLD snapshot takes about 160 ms from the
host's game to the member's (the session of 2026-10-28), longer than the delay itself, so the
cursor was always past the newest pose: a figure ran on along its velocity, was held, and was
pulled forward when the next pose came; a moby (WORLD has no velocities) stood still and jumped,
15 times a second. A moby…

commits.headline: feat(multiplayer): the verbose log says how remote poses arrive and are shown
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
Each pose and WORLD snapshot received with its stamp, its stamp in this game's clock, when it
came and its transit; twice a second each figure's buffer (delay, transit, jitter, interval,
loss, how far ahead the newest pose is) and what its frames showed (between two poses, ahead,
held, jumped), with the clock's round trip and offset; once a second the same for the host's
mobys driven here, and how many of them something else moved after they were put in place.

commits.headline: feat(multiplayer): OPENRAC_MP_LAG holds received messages back, to test a slow link
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
OPENRAC_MP_LAG="<ms>[,<jitter ms>]" delays each message the server sent by that much more, plus
a random extra of about the jitter, in the order they came, so a party on one machine plays as
over the internet.

commits.headline: chore(multiplayer): version 0.7.2
commits.author: Veradictus

commits.headline: fix(multiplayer): a standing figure no longer bobs
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A grounded Ratchet's velocity says he falls at 0.749 units a second (the game's gravity, which
the ground takes back each tick; tests/data/pose_stall.csv), while his z stands. Whenever a pose
came late and the cursor ran past the newest one, the figure was carried down along that velocity
for up to 150 ms (about 0.1 units) and eased back up when the next pose came: the up and down
vibration seen through game.openrac.dev. Along an axis on which two poses did not move (less
than 0.01 units),…

commits.headline: feat(multiplayer): the verbose log has each received pose's place and this hero's z each tick
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A pose received is logged with its position, velocity and state, and twice a second this game's
hero with the range of his z over the ticks, how many ticks it changed, where he is and his
velocity: whether a sender's z flickers shows in the next trace.

commits.headline: fix(multiplayer): a bolt taken by another player flies to them before it goes
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A bolt that had landed runs by itself in each game, so the claim, the
host's own pickup and DESPAWN removed it at once in the games that
watched. The host now says who took a bolt (TAKEN, kind 24); each game
where it hovers by itself has it fly to that player, the taker's figure
standing in for the hero during its update so the game's own pickup
flight plays, and lets the bolt update delete it on arrival with nothing
added. DESPAWN and KILLED leave such a bolt to its flight, and one that
has…

commits.headline: fix(multiplayer): a figure's held item animates between poses as its body does
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A held item's seq, key, time and speed came with each pose, but the
figure was given the nearer pose's as they were, so its item's key only
moved when a pose came and the port's speed nudging hunted. Each piece
both poses have now runs on from the one's key and time to the other's
every frame, as the body's animation does, a new seq or a blend keeping
the nearer pose's; a thrown wrench moves along between its two places.

commits.headline: fix(multiplayer): a bolt flying to whoever took it runs wherever the camera is
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A taken bolt's flight is its own update, which a game runs only near
its camera (or an eye). Each game now puts an eye on every bolt flying
to another player, so the flight plays, and clears them once none fly.
